correctness.rationale: Uniform \(d\)-step multiplication gives \(P+n^{-1/2}C+n^{-1}D+O(n^{-3/2})\). The centered Poisson-response row solves \(w(I-P)=\pi C\), \(w\mathbf1=0\). Primitive-block contraction gives normalized rows \(\pi+n^{-1/2}w+O(n^{-1})\). Survival normalized multipliers equal \(1+\beta/n+O(n^{-3/2})\), with \(\beta=\pi D\mathbf1+wC\mathbf1\), and their logarithmic products have positive limits after \(n^{-\beta/d}\) normalization. Exact rational code checks \(\pi C\mathbf1=0\), the Poisson equation, the direct and response terms and \(\beta\) for both cyclic classes and both phases; finite slopes agree. All source hypotheses and fixed starting-time/phase quantifiers appear in RESULT.md; numeric tests do not prove infinite convergence.

originality.rationale: The full primary Iba preprint treats phase-independent \(1/n\) perturbations, so its universal kappa formula does not cover centered periodic \(n^{-1/2}\) perturbations or the different-class exponents. The full Champagnat–Villemonais manuscript treats time-homogeneous periodics. Targeted literature and mathematical-record comparisons did not find the Markov-specific Poisson-response formula together with exact opposite class exponents. Classical Benzaid–Lutz abstract linear-difference asymptotics are a residual priority risk, not a confirmed statement implying the specific quantitative theorem.

value.rationale: The 2026 motivating survival theorem supplies a natural first-order universality expectation and leaves critical square-root, zero-average perturbations outside its assumptions. The result gives a new second-order Green/Poisson-response invariant and an explicit four-state boundary in which starting classes have opposite algebraic survival corrections despite the same exponential rate. This quantitative phase distinction is invisible to ordinary spectral decay, is nontrivial beyond direct averaging and is mathematically useful for near-critical survival comparisons.
